en: The Twenty-One Verses of Homage to Vajrayoginī.
Om. Homage to the glorious Vajrayoginī! Seated in the form of the syllable Evaṃ.
O you whose form is innate bliss,
who abide within the body of wisdom-consciousness,
homage to you, Vajrayoginī! 1.
O you whose body consists of the four joys through the manifestation of the Vicitra and other stages,
who have attained the perfection of passion— homage to you, Vajrayoginī! (2)
Homage to you, O Vajrayoginī, who resemble the full moon of autumn, who are born from the union with the eightfold group of beings, and who arise from the primordial seed-syllable of all colors. 3.

Homage to you, O Vajrayoginī, who transcend the duality of existence and non-existence, who are devoid of beginning, middle, and end, and who are liberated from the distinction between self and other. 4.
Homage to you, Vajrayoginī, who are the union of passion and dispassion, free from the three types of conceptualization, and the bringer of the bliss of great bliss. 5.
Homage to you, O Vajrayoginī, who are engaged in accomplishing the welfare of sentient beings, who have manifested in a form of enjoyment, and whose body is dyed with compassion. 6.
Homage to you, Vajrayoginī, who has ascended from existence to nirvāṇa, who is resplendent with the forms of all phenomena, and who is the eye of body, speech, and mind. (7)
Holding a skull-cup and a khaṭvāṅga in your left hands and a flaying knife in your right, you who embody emptiness and compassion—homage to you, Vajrayoginī! (8)
O you who terrify those difficult for even the Jinas to subdue, O destroyer of all Māras,
O supreme one who has conquered all enemies— homage to you, Vajrayoginī! (9)
O you who are endowed with the [eight] arts (kalāpa), who dwell in the eight cremation grounds, and who are joined with the flavors of the Buddha’s dance— homage to you, Vajrayoginī! 10.
O Vajrayoginī, who manifests in many forms created solely according to the inclinations of sentient beings, appearing with dark, yellow, and white radiance—homage to you! 11.
Born from the five Buddha-families and having attained the state of the five yoginīs, likewise numbering as many as atoms—homage to you, O Vajrayoginī! (12)
Homage to you, O Vajrayoginī, who are celebrated as Śakti in the Śaiva tradition, conceived as Caṇḍī in the sacred ford, and renowned as Veda in the Veda.
Homage to you, O Vajrayoginī, who are known as Kulā and celebrated as Kubjikā; who are considered to possess the form of the Self; who are the universal form and the embodiment of action. 14.
Because it contradicts the view of a self, it does not lead to the production [of existence].
Homage to you, Vajrayoginī, who are endowed with the excellence of all aspects! 15.

Homage to you, Vajrayoginī, whose sole sphere of experience is the vision of the profound yoga of the selflessness of phenomena, and who transcends all conceptualizations of existence and non-existence. 16.
O Mother Prajñāpāramitā, free from dark, yellow, and other colors, devoid of both color and non-color; homage to you, O Vajrayoginī! (17)
Homage to you, Vajrayoginī, who are non-conceptual, without support, free from proliferation, without abode, all-pervading like space, and devoid of self. 18.
O Mother Vajrayoginī, the vessel for all who possess the knowledge of jewels;
homage to you, Vajravārāhī; homage to you, Vajrayoginī. (19)
You have emerged from the lotus-face of the true guru, assuming forms at will;
salutations to you, Vajrayoginī, for the destruction of great ignorance! (20)
By means of the merit obtained from thus performing the twenty-one-fold rite for a mother endowed with such virtues, may all people attain perfection. || 21 ||
The *Śrīvajrayoginīpraṇāmaikaviṃśikā* (The Twenty-One Homages to Śrī Vajrayoginī) is complete.
